workbookPolicy: Current main sole reference. All selected profiles/description-only evidence considered without an outline quota. No workbook regeneration or edits. Historical outlines do not override formal prerequisites or future offerings.

courses.name: Personal & Professional Development
courses.contributionFinding: Required personal, ethical and academic development; reflection on societal engagement, writing and independent learning. Supports GROW-type development but is broader and has more credit.

courses.name: AI Ethics
courses.contributionFinding: Ethical frameworks applied to fairness,privacy,responsibility,moralstatus andpolitical risks ofAI directly examine contemporary applied ethics. Psychological andorganisational perspectives support inquiry into humanity andagency; research synthesis andapodcast retain explicitmethod limits.

courses.name: Logic & Discrete Mathematics
courses.contributionFinding: Propositions,quantifiers,validinference,Booleanalgebra andformal proof provide direct logic andargument-validity training. The additional discrete mathematics andgame-strategy material is not described as philosophicalmethodology.

courses.name: Machine Learning
courses.contributionFinding: Statisticallearning,prediction,model validation andmethodlimits supply concrete computational models against which artificialinference and empirical explanation can be examined. No machineconsciousness or philosophical theory is claimed as its syllabus.

courses.name: Introduction to Programming
courses.contributionFinding: provides computational foundations for examining artificial systems and representation

courses.name: Law, Society & Justice
courses.contributionFinding: introduces law, social order and competing conceptions of justice

courses.name: Modern History
courses.contributionFinding: Industrialisation,political ideologies,imperialism anddecolonisation provide specific historical developments against which modern political and cultural arguments can be interpreted. The course remains history,not a dedicated modern-philosophy sequence.

courses.name: Histories of Gender
courses.contributionFinding: Intersectional histories ofgender,sexuality,family,incarceration andactivism provide specific historical cases for arguments about identity,equality,exclusion and agency. They do not substitute for a philosophical-history sequence.

courses.name: Native American Histories
courses.contributionFinding: Indigenous historical perspectives,relational accountability,reciprocity andknowledge-holder collaboration provide a specific complementary case for examining knowledge,ethical relationships and marginalised accounts of personhood andcommunity. This does not claim a systematic Indigenous-philosophy syllabus.

courses.name: Human Rights: Law & Philosophy
courses.contributionFinding: examines philosophical foundations and legal expression of human rights

courses.name: Criminal Law & Criminal Justice
courses.contributionFinding: studies responsibility, punishment and justice through criminal law

courses.name: Comparative Constitutional Law
courses.contributionFinding: compares constitutional arrangements, rights and distributions of political authority

courses.name: Foundations of European Union Law
courses.contributionFinding: examines the legal and institutional foundations of European political order

courses.name: Introduction to Western Philosophy
courses.contributionFinding: Philosophical arguments about knowledge,ethics,God,mind,freedom,identity,time and meaning provide a disciplinary foundation across historical and contemporary thought. Close argument analysis and essays directly implement philosophical study.

courses.name: Ethics
courses.contributionFinding: Moral theories and close philosophical reading include Kant,utilitarianism,virtue ethics,contractarianism,feminist ethics,Nietzsche,Murdoch andNagel. Essays develop interpretation,argument evaluation and independent ethical positions; no dedicated climate-ethics syllabus is asserted.

courses.name: Philosophy of Mind
courses.contributionFinding: Historical and contemporary arguments about minds,selves,conscious experience,identity and the mind-body problem directly address philosophical anthropology and psychology. Essays also examine machineconsciousness,perception and the value of experience.

courses.name: Philosophy of Emotion
courses.contributionFinding: Competing philosophical theories of emotion connect feelings to knowledge,decision-making,ethics,social life and politics. Textual analysis and an independent argument engage moralpsychology and rationality directly.

courses.name: Free Will, Time & the Self
courses.contributionFinding: Greek and Indian approaches to free will,determinism,moral responsibility,time andself directly engage metaphysics and humanagency. Close source analysis and independent essays provide advanced philosophical argument.

courses.name: Introduction to Political Philosophy
courses.contributionFinding: European and non-European political thought examines human nature,society,rights andauthority through originaltexts and normative argument. This supplies direct political-philosophy and historical thought,not merely empirical institutional context.

courses.name: Foundations of Comparative Politics
courses.contributionFinding: provides comparative frameworks for political institutions and power

courses.name: Theory of International Relations
courses.contributionFinding: tests political theories, norms and explanatory arguments in international relations

courses.name: European Union Politics
courses.contributionFinding: examines political institutions, authority and choices in European governance

courses.name: Peace & Conflict
courses.contributionFinding: asks how conflict arises and how peacebuilding may be justified

courses.name: Qualitative Research Methodology
courses.contributionFinding: provides qualitative interpretive methods for investigating contemporary social questions

courses.name: Modern Sociology
courses.contributionFinding: Phenomenology,critical theory,Blackfeminist thought,Bourdieu andpostcolonial perspectives supply concrete social theories ofmodernity,power andexclusion. Their comparison supports political/social-philosophy questions while remaining socialtheory.

courses.name: Social Movements & Environmental Justice
courses.contributionFinding: examines collective action, environmental justice and marginalisation

courses.name: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
courses.contributionFinding: Critical,neofunctionalist anddecolonial theories ofcivil society,trust,hegemony,solidarity andpublicspheres supply specific frameworks for socialphilosophy. The independent research project is not described as mandatory NGO fieldwork.

courses.name: Neurobiology
courses.contributionFinding: grounds questions about mind and representation in neural systems

courses.name: Perception & Action
courses.contributionFinding: studies how perception and action connect mental representation to the world

courses.name: Higher Order Functions
courses.contributionFinding: studies advanced cognition and higher-order mental functions

courses.name: Psycholinguistics
courses.contributionFinding: examines the relation between language processing, cognition and the brain

courses.name: Introduction to Brain & Behavior
courses.contributionFinding: introduces brain, behaviour and cognition as empirical perspectives on mind and human nature

courses.name: Social Psychology
courses.contributionFinding: Social cognition, the self, influence, group processes, prejudice, aggression and prosocial behaviour provide empirical perspectives on persons and moral/social judgment. Research synthesis and study design do not substitute for philosophical moral argument.

courses.name: Statistics & Experimental Methods
courses.contributionFinding: develops experimental and statistical methods for claims about mind and behaviour

courses.name: Advanced Research Methods & Statistics
courses.contributionFinding: Systematic review,metaanalysis,effect sizes,bias,heterogeneity anduncertainty give specific tools for evaluating empirical claims about mind andbehaviour. This is complementary evidencesynthesis,not a philosophy seminar or guaranteed originalcognitiveexperiment.

courses.name: The Art of Rhetorical Communication
courses.contributionFinding: Classical rhetoric,persuasive appeals,argumentation andfallacies directly exercise critical examination andconstruction ofarguments. This is complementary argumentative practice,not a philosophy-specific methodology course.

courses.name: Style & Meaning
courses.contributionFinding: Linguistic choices,discourse,cognition,modality andperspective are related to literary meaning through substantive stylistic analysis. This complements inquiry into interpretation andlanguage,without replacing philosophical semantics.

courses.name: Persuasive Communication
courses.contributionFinding: Framing,argumentation,cognitive shortcuts andethical influence are critically investigated through literature andreflective research. This gives a specific applied case for examining persuasion,rational agency and public judgment,not generic presentation-skills credit.

courses.name: Heritage & Ancient Democracy
courses.contributionFinding: Athenian citizenship,exclusion,crises anddeliberation are studied through texts andmaterialevidence. They provide a concrete historical case for evaluating democracy andpolitical equality,not a general substitute for ancient philosophy.

courses.name: Introduction to Literary Studies
courses.contributionFinding: introduces theories and methods for interpreting language, texts and meaning

courses.name: Great Literary Works
courses.contributionFinding: Texts from ancient epic to modernfiction explicitly examine humanity,mortality,gender,freedom,community andcivilisation,including philosophicalsatire. This is specific literary material for philosophical interpretation,not a history-of-philosophy course.

courses.name: World Myth & Literature
courses.contributionFinding: Creation,power,gender,love andloyalty are compared across mythic traditions using theories of myth and literary analysis. These representations supply specific complementary material for philosophical anthropology and cultural interpretation,not epistemology or philosophical history by substitution.

courses.name: Perspectives on Literary Meaning
courses.contributionFinding: examines theories of meaning and interpretation through close reading

concepts.label: Philosophy, society & interpretation
concepts.concept: Philosophical inquiry into knowledge, ethics, mind, agency and political authority is supported by logic, critical social theory and interpretation of historical and literary texts. Social psychology provides a specific empirical perspective on persons and moral judgment. The programme combines philosophical reading and argument with interdisciplinary cases while retaining important specialist gaps.

concepts.label: Ethics, politics, justice and institutions
concepts.concept: Ethics, political philosophy, logic and human-rights reasoning examine responsibility, justice, freedom and authority. Law, social theory, gender history and literary interpretation provide specific institutions, social experiences and arguments through which those normative questions can be assessed.

concepts.label: Mind, language, cognition and artificial intelligence
concepts.concept: Philosophy of mind, emotion, agency and ethical responsibility is examined alongside empirical cognition, language and neuroscience. Logic, programming and statistical methods provide complementary ways to assess representation, artificial inference and competing evidence about mental life. Empirical training does not replace philosophical argument.

academicChallenge.closest: All five philosophy courses, political philosophy, formal logic, human rights and applied AI ethics provide sustained philosophical subject matter and argument/reading practice across ethics, mind, agency and politics. Historical/literary interpretation and critical social theory are specific complements; their coherence alone does not establish comparability. Missing dedicated epistemology/science/history/methods sequences remain real limitations. The direct philosophical core plus these evidenced complements materially responds to defining target substance; no equivalence or matching-course quota used.
academicChallenge.politicalSocial: Normative philosophical core remains; law adds responsibility, punishment, rights and constitutional authority; sociology and social movements add power, exclusion and collective action. Modern current history seminar would not implement this concept, so replaced by formal logic. Literary perspectives supply concrete interpretive frameworks, not generic rhetoric.
academicChallenge.mindLanguage: Philosophical mind/emotion/agency/ethics retained alongside empirical brain, language and cognition; computing/model evaluation provides distinct explanatory approaches and limitations. These methods support this target pillar without claiming they are philosophical semantics or replace argument.
academicChallenge.stopping: All three passed in order with 8/11/14 course differences; formal Entrepreneurship candidate recorded maximum-reached, not falsely rejected or fabricated as fourth.

alignments.rationale: Introduction to Western Philosophy studies ancient sources and later philosophical arguments. This is a direct partial philosophical-history relationship; a complete ancient-and-medieval survey is not claimed.
UCR Ethics includes Kant and close philosophical reading, but is already assigned to introductory ethics. It is not repeated as an identical dedicated six-EC Kant course.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces Tilburg’s dedicated Kritiek van de Instrumentele Rede component.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces Tilburg’s dedicated Existentialisme en Structuralisme component.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces Tilburg’s dedicated Hedendaagse Fenomenologie component.
Modern History provides historical context, but its primary subject is not the history of philosophical arguments. The dedicated modern-philosophy component is kept separate.
The removed archaeology course supplied contextual material, not direct cultural-philosophy study. Specific literary and social-theory complements remain, without a forced component match.
Ethics directly examines moral theories, duties and judgments central to Tilburg’s compulsory Ethics course.
Introduction to Political Philosophy directly examines normative political questions central to Tilburg’s Political Philosophy course.

AI Ethics explicitly applies ethical frameworks to fairness, privacy, responsibility and moral status. It supplies a direct contemporary applied-ethics relationship without matching every Tilburg application.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces Tilburg’s dedicated Hedendaagse Sociale en Politieke Filosofie component.
European Union Politics studies empirical institutions and policymaking. The current evidence does not establish the primary philosophical content of this dedicated Political Topics course.
Philosophy of Mind directly addresses consciousness, personal identity and mind–body relations.

Philosophy of Emotion directly examines emotion, knowledge, moral judgment and action. These are identifiable parts of moral psychology; the course also covers wider emotional and aesthetic experience.
Free Will, Time & the Self addresses metaphysical questions about time, agency and personal identity, while narrower than Tilburg’s general Metaphysics course.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces Tilburg’s dedicated Wijsgerige Antropologie component.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces Tilburg’s dedicated Epistemologie component.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces Tilburg’s dedicated Wetenschapsfilosofie component.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces Tilburg’s dedicated Analytische Filosofie component.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces Tilburg’s dedicated Philosophy of Language component.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces Tilburg’s dedicated Society, Science and Information component.
Propositional and quantified logic, valid inference and proof directly address formal reasoning. The additional mathematical material is not treated as a full philosophical-argumentation syllabus.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces Tilburg’s dedicated Academisch Nederlands 1 component.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces Tilburg’s dedicated Academisch Nederlands 2 component.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces Tilburg’s dedicated Bachelorscriptietraject component.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces Tilburg’s dedicated Scriptie component.
Rhetorical argument and speaking support communication, but a dedicated philosophical-research presentation component is not established.
Literary interpretation and philosophical essays support related analytical work, but no scheduled course establishes the specific styles of philosophical methodology taught here.
Personal & Professional Development supports reflection, collaboration and planning similar to GROW mentoring, while broader and carrying more credit.
This is genuine 30-EC choice space. No fixed subject or fictional UCR counterpart is assigned.

alignmentFinding: All 30 components and 43 UCR codes accounted for once per applicable programme; 9 partial substantive relationships, 21 deliberate blanks. Removed contextual archaeology/history and generic teaching/method/presentation alignments. Strongest adequate subject relationship retained; equivalence not required. Optional 15 EC independent research aligned with thesis separately, outside schedules and 180 EC.
